packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-04 - unverified image reading (reader C)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or prior reading of this material was in my context. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the brief: the images are very dark, so I made local derivative copies of the packet images
  (greyscale, contrast stretch, slight gamma, some crops) with a small PIL script in my scratchpad.
  All readings come from the supplied images or those derivatives. I opened no other file, catalogue,
  edition, web or search tool, and I did not open packet.json.

OVERALL VERDICT
- Partial, low-confidence reading. The leaf is darkened, stained and abraded. The tiles are strongly
  enlarged relative to the detail actually captured, so letter forms are soft at tile scale. The script
  is a small, heavily abbreviated academic book hand, and many abbreviation signs cannot be resolved
  at this resolution. I could fix some recurring words but no secure connected span of ten or more
  lines. Every word below is queried unless noted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- One face (image-001 overview). This is a parchment leaf or bifolium reused as a limp binding wrapper.
  A spine band runs horizontally across the middle of the image with three sewing-support stations,
  and there is a small modern paper label "3" (or "S") at the right end of the spine band. Upper and
  lower halves are the covers; the text is upright in the image.
- Writing: four narrow text columns across the width. There is a vertical gutter or fold at about
  x = 50% of the overview, so these are probably two pages side by side with two columns each
  (tentative). The text survives in rectangular blocks separated by blank or abraded horizontal bands
  at about y = 33-37%, 46-48% (spine), 67-72% and 75-80%. Those bands are probably wear from the folds
  and turn-ins, not original layout (tentative).
- Paragraph marks, some red (capitulum signs), appear at block and line starts, e.g. upper col. 3
  near the top and lower col. 3 left edge (024). Several small enlarged initials with flourishes.
- Upper centre, near the gutter: a later note in a different, cursive hand, written in three short
  stacked lines with fraction-like strokes (around overview x 540-600, y 250-300). It may be a shelfmark
  or numerals. Not read.
- Lower left, at about y = 1180 of the overview: a short line set off in a box or at the line end,
  reading "?gr(ati)a/?g(e)n(er)is ?d(e)l(?)" (unclear). It may be a catchword or a marginal addition.
- No interlinear glosses identified. I see nothing that clearly separates lemma from commentary.
  Tentative impression: continuous scholastic prose.

TILE MAP (inferred from tile sizes; positions approximate)
- 002-007: top-left quadrant (pairs left/right, three rows).   008-013: top-right quadrant.
- 014-019: bottom-left quadrant.                               020-025: bottom-right quadrant.
- 020 and 021 fall mostly on the blank or stained area right of the spine (little text).

SELECTED SPANS
"L" = line of writing counted from the top of the named image. ( ) = expansion. ? = uncertain reading.

--- Lower block, col. 3 (top of block = image-022 lower half; continues in 024) ---

022 L6   [paraph] ?a(?) ?d(?) ?ca(?) [illegible] ?ip(s)a ?d(?)
(022 L6 onward = 024 L1 onward, overlap)

Note: the word I mark "?aff(?)" occurs several times with a tall double s/f ligature. It may be "affirmatiua",
"affectio" or "assignatio"; I cannot decide which at this resolution. Treat it as unread.

--- Upper block, col. 2, lower lines (image-005 upper part) ---

Note: "finis" (or "f(or)mis/f(or)ma") is the most stable recurring word in this block. It also seems
to appear in the overview at about x 440, y 437 and in the lower-left block.

--- Lower block, col. 1 (image-019) ---

(this block's last line appears to end at 019 L15; a large flourish "2"-shaped mark follows below, probably
a catchword flourish, a line filler or a quire mark)

--- Lower block, col. 2 (image-018) ---
018 L4   ?ea(?) ?d(?) ?ab ?sit(?) ?b

018 L6   ?a(?) ?actu(?) ?(con)tinuu(m)(?) ?z [illegible]

018 L11  ?ex ?ita(?) ?p(?) ?b ?actu(?)/?acc(ide)n(s)(?) ?d(?)
018 L12  ?b ?d(?) ?sunt(?) ?d(?) ?d(?)
018 L13-16 [illegible, faded]

UNREAD AREAS
- Top-left quadrant above 005: tiles 002-004 are very dark. I looked at them but transcribed nothing
  secure.
- Top-right quadrant (008-013): only looked at 009. Its text is dense but very soft, and I read nothing
  secure. A darker paraph-led passage at the lower left of 009 begins "?q(uod) ?a(?) ... ?p(ro)/?po ...",
  but I could not read it.
- Col. 4, lower block (lower right of the overview; tiles 024-025 right edge and 025): not
  transcribed.
- Spine-band text (overview y about 880-930) and the later cursive note near the gutter: not read.

SUGGESTIONS
- A native-resolution capture (these tiles look upsampled) or a multispectral/UV capture is needed.
  The most promising blocks for a re-shoot are lower col. 3 (022/024) and lower col. 4 (lower right of
  the overview), where the ink is darkest.

LIMITATIONS
- Column order and page order (which half is front cover) are not established.
- Recurring words I'm moderately confident about: "finis" (005), "actu" (018/019), "species" (022/024),
  "quod", "esse". Everything else is tentative. Do not search on single readings without re-checking.
